artifacts.layman_summary: Collects eight published temperature-over-time records of hot coffee, tea or water cooling in cups and pots, all put in one standard format so later tests can check cooling models against them.
artifacts.name: gen_art_dataset_1
artifacts.summary: This artifact is the held-out evidence set for the next iteration's test of Newton-type cooling models for hot liquids. It collects eight published cooling curves from three independent sources and standardizes them to one JSON schema (exp_sel_data_out): one source group per dataset, one example per curve, and metadata_fold giving the source index so each source can be held out as one fold. The sources are: Sedlacek and Dolejsi (2010), a measured coffee curve in a china pot (Fig. 1, digitized from vector markers, 0 to 138 min, stated measurement error 0.3 C); a University of Manitoba workshop coffee table (0 to 48 min, Fahrenheit converted to Celsius, room temperature 71 F); and Langer, Winkler and Lachenmeier (2018), six single-use 237 mL cup curves for hot water at 88 C (0 to 33 min, digitized from vector polylines, CC-BY-4.0 Zenodo record). The Langer paper's other four curves were digitized but left out to stay within the eight-curve target. No fits or derived statistics are computed. Each example records the initial temperature, room temperature where reported, cup and volume, lid or fat-layer condition where reported, and a provenance block with citation, URL, source type, measurement error and digitization method and error. Coverage limits are recorded: no source reports relative humidity (0 of 3), no measured fat-layer series is present, and the Langer digitized 65 C crossing times (18 to 32 min) disagree with the paper's own text (11 to 22 min), which is flagged and unresolved. The search was a convenience sample of about fifteen queries, not a systematic review. Outputs are full_data_out.json, mini_data_out.json and preview_data_out.json, validated against the schema with zero errors, and a pinned .venv with reproducibility.md gives the exact rerun steps.
artifacts.title: Published hot-liquid cooling curves for held-out tests

artifacts.layman_summary: We digitized a published coffee-cooling curve and checked how well Newton's simple cooling law predicts the first 30 minutes. The simple law misses by about one degree, and the paper's own reported statistics could not be reproduced.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_1
artifacts.summary: Screens cooling models on the digitized china-pot coffee curve of Sedlacek and Dolejsi (29 measured points, 0-139 min, read from the vector figures of the source PDF; digitization disagreement 0.15 C, below the stated 0.3 C thermometer error). Baseline: constant-rate Newton law (C0), fitted on the first 30 minutes (7 points, last at 25.9 min): in-sample 30-minute RMS 1.07 K, 95% block-bootstrap interval 0.60-1.53 K, with systematic early underprediction (+0.62 K over 0-10 min) and late overprediction (-0.87 K). Extensions: nonlinear convection C1 (exponent 1.94 in-window, 1.68 full record) gives 0.36 K in-sample; the two-term evaporation forms collapse to C1 (evaporation not identifiable). The source's drawn model-1 curve scores 2.42 K over the same window. Reproduction gate FAILED: the source's chi2/NDF values (32.1, 2.4, 81.3, 1.0) are not reproduced from its own drawn curves (0.03-0.29 of reported), so the pre-registered selection rule was not applied. Humidity, pot geometry, the metal and vacuum pots and the fat-covered control are not testable from the source. Validation: T1, T2, T4, T7 pass; T3, T5, T6 fail and are reported. An independent re-derivation from the raw PDF reproduces the headline RMS values within 0.003 K; a permutation placebo gives p = 0.01 for the C1-over-C0 improvement. Outputs: method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out schema, validated), full/mini/preview versions, three figures, README.md, reproducibility.md.
artifacts.title: Testing Newton's cooling law on published coffee curves

artifacts.layman_summary: This screen checks published studies for how well the simple cooling rule for hot drinks matches real measurements, and whether those studies recorded room humidity or the weight lost to evaporation.
artifacts.name: gen_art_research_1
artifacts.summary: Web-only literature screen of how accurately Newton's law of cooling predicts hot-coffee temperature over time, and whether open-cup studies record ambient humidity or cup mass loss alongside cooling curves. Verified: the Vollmer (2009) abstract states that simple exponential (Newton) cooling is mostly valid below a temperature-difference threshold that depends on experimental conditions, and that larger differences show appreciable deviations because radiation is not linear in temperature difference; that study uses solid objects up to 300 K, not coffee. Verified: Luniachek et al. (2017) use ambient humidity only as an input to a theoretical evaporation model, not as a measured cooling-curve variable. Not verified: the Sedláček and Dolejší pot study (search snippet: chi-squared per degree of freedom falling from 32.1 to 2.4 with an evaporation term), a 2025 CFD small-cup paper (snippet: omitting evaporation significantly underpredicts cooling), a 2025 radiation paper, a soup-bowl humidity study (snippet: evaporation higher by day than at night), and an IOP paper on evaporative and convective mechanisms. These were blocked (HTTP 403, TLS error or no text), so their claims rest on snippets only, and no number from a snippet is used. Conclusion: no verified source gives a measured 30-minute accuracy figure for a coffee cup, and no verified source records humidity or cup mass loss alongside curves. This is an absence in what could be read, not proof that no such study exists. Confidence is low; the answer would change with full text of the blocked sources.
artifacts.title: Newton's law vs published coffee-cup cooling data

critiques.description: The report says the source's drawn model-1 curve shows the same early-under, late-over residual pattern as the constant-rate law, and 'What we have learned' repeats this as support. Table 1 gives the drawn curve +0.99 K over 0-10 min and +2.49 K over 20 min and later; residual_series_window gives +3.48 K at 20.9 min and +1.50 K at 25.9 min. Its late residuals are positive, while C0's late mean is -0.87 K. The claim is therefore contradicted by the record's own table, and T6's interpretation depends on it.
critiques.suggested_action: Remove the claim, or restate it as what the table shows: the drawn curve overpredicts at both early and late points, which is a different pattern from C0. Then say the T6 excess (6.9 times the digitization error) is not explained by the source's model. Re-check every sentence that cites the drawn curve.

critiques.description: The statement that the constant-rate law 'fits the whole record well only when T_room is free' is contradicted by Table 2. With T_room free, C0 has RSS/NDF 0.84 K^2. At sigma = 0.3 C (0.09 K^2) that is chi2/NDF of about 9, against about 0.8 for C1 with T_room fixed. Only the C1 fit is consistent with the measurement error.
critiques.suggested_action: Rewrite the sentence to say that freeing T_room lowers the C0 RSS/NDF from 9.2 to 0.84 K^2 but leaves it about nine times the measurement variance, while C1 stays near 0.8 under either choice. Keep the ambient-temperature dependence as a separate finding.

critiques.description: The headline 'C0 30-minute RMS about 1.1 K' is conditional on T_room = 20 C, which the source does not report, and the report's own sensitivity fit shows it depends strongly on that choice: freeing T_room gives C0 RMS 0.54 K with T_room at its 35 C bound. The 'What we have learned' section states 1.1 K without that condition, so the constant-rate misfit it reports is closer to an assumption than a measurement.
critiques.suggested_action: State the 1.1 K figure as conditional on T_room = 20 C everywhere it appears, including the summary, and give the free-ambient figure (0.54 K) beside it. Say that the constant-rate misfit is not established independently of the ambient assumption, and frame the held-out test as the way to settle it.

critiques.description: The 'late overprediction' of C0 and the sign change between about 21 and 26 minutes rest on two window points. At 20.9 min the C0 residual is +0.30 K, and at 25.9 min it is -2.03 K, which alone gives the -0.87 K late mean. The seven-point window cannot establish a late shape, and the report presents it as the shape the hypothesis predicted.
critiques.suggested_action: Say explicitly that the late sign depends on one point (25.9 min), and that the early pattern rests on the 3.1, 5.0 and 10.0 min points. Do not describe the shape as confirming the hypothesis until the held-out curves are scored.

critiques.description: The exponent of the nonlinear law moves across the fits the report presents: x = 1.94 in the window, 1.68 full-record with T_room fixed, 1.82 full-record with T_room free, and 1.50 in the window with T_room free. The report discusses the RMS stability under ambient choice but not the instability of x, which bears directly on whether C1 is a stable model of the curve or a flexible fit to seven points.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a short paragraph and a row set listing x and a for each fit, and state that the exponent is not stable across windows and ambient choices. Say what this implies for claiming C1 as the better model.

critiques.description: The positive claim, that a nonlinear convection term fits the first 30 minutes better than the constant-rate law, is not compared with its nearest published neighbour. The report cites Vollmer (2009) for the fact that Newton's law deviates at large temperature differences and needs a nonlinear treatment, and the source's own model 1 already includes nonlinear terms. The record does not say what this iteration adds beyond those results.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a short comparison: Vollmer (2009) reports that the exponential law holds only below a threshold and that radiation drives the deviation; the source already reports a nonlinear model. State that this iteration adds a single-curve, in-sample quantification of the 30-minute misfit with a bootstrap interval and a failed reproduction gate, and nothing about generality. Do not credit novelty until this is written.

critiques.description: The original question asks how accurately Newton's law predicts a coffee cup over 30 minutes, compared with published measurements. The run answers this in-sample on one curve (seven window points, 29 total). The eight-curve held-out set, which includes a second coffee curve (Manitoba), is collected but not scored, so no out-of-sample accuracy and no comparison across published measurements exists yet. The humidity, fat-layer and geometry parts of the hypothesis are not testable with this evidence.
critiques.suggested_action: Score C0 and C1 on the held-out curves (Manitoba coffee first, then the Langer hot-water curves) in the next iteration, and report out-of-sample RMS beside the in-sample figures. Until then, state in the report that the question is partly answered, and do not present the in-sample 1.1 K as an accuracy figure for a coffee cup in general.

critiques.description: The reproduction-gate targets (32.1, 2.4, 81.3 and 1.0 chi2/NDF) are hard-coded in src/analysis.py (line 249) and the report gives no location for them in the source (page, table or figure). The literature screen says the 32.1 and 2.4 values came from an unverified search snippet and that no number from a snippet is used. The gate's failure, which blocks the selection rule, depends entirely on these values, so their provenance has to be recorded.
critiques.suggested_action: State where in the source PDF each of the four values appears (table, figure or page), with the text quoted, or state that they are from a snippet and unverified. If they are unverified, say that the gate result is conditional on them. Name the source's drawn-curve figure (Fig. 1 or Fig. 2) for the reproduction check.

critiques.description: The placebo and the independent re-derivation are attributed to [ARTIFACT:art_UaVOg91elcVt] without naming their file. Their numbers are in results/audit.json, and the gate note points to analysis_results.json. T5 uses 200 bootstrap replicates, which the report does not state. The re-derivation's 0.003 K figure is for the published curve (2.419 against 2.422), not the fitted models (both agree to 0.00002 K); the report's sentence does not say so.
critiques.suggested_action: Name results/audit.json, results/tests.json and results/analysis_results.json wherever these claims appear. State the T5 replicate count, and say which values the 0.003 K agreement covers.

critiques.description: Two citations have no entry in the report's bibliography. Luniachek et al. (2017) appears in the text and as [6] in the screen's sources, but the bibliography lists only [1] and [2]. Reference [1] (Sedlacek and Dolejsi) has no venue, and the report states that no BibTeX entry was written. The paper step cannot cite either source from the report as it stands.
critiques.suggested_action: Add Luniachek et al. (2017) to the bibliography with its DOI or URL and its verification status, and record the Sedlacek and Dolejsi venue or mark it unverified, so the paper step does not invent one.

critiques.description: The held-out dataset is described only by a summary table. Its eight curves (their ids, sample counts, time spans and initial temperatures) are not listed in the report, although they are the evidence the next iteration will use. The report also says Langer's 65 C crossing times disagree with the source's own text but does not state which curves this affects.
critiques.suggested_action: List the eight curves in a table in the report, with their dataset ids and the Langer curves flagged for the unresolved crossing-time disagreement. Why: the next iteration's test set must be identifiable from the record alone.

dimension_scores.justification: The drawn-curve residual claim contradicts Table 1 and analysis_results.json (residual_series_window): the source's model-1 curve has residuals of +0.99 K (0-10 min) and +2.49 K (20 min and later), both positive, so it does not show the late-negative shape that C0 shows. The record uses this claim to support the reading of T6 and as a learned result. The free-ambient claim that C0 'fits the whole record well' is also contradicted by Table 2 (RSS/NDF 0.84 K^2 against a 0.09 K^2 measurement variance). The headline 1.1 K misfit is conditional on an unreported ambient temperature that the record does not state alongside it. The rest of the numerical work is sound and reproduces.

Chronological, with each section stating what it tested and what came out. Tables are introduced by their purpose and the figure markers have captions. Some passages mix sources: the drawn curve is called Fig. 1 in the report but Fig. 2 in method_out.json, and the window end time is 138.5 min in one table and 138.9 min in another without explanation.

Most of the run is preserved: the three artifacts, all validation checks T1 to T7, the sensitivity and forecast fits, and the dead ends. What is missing is the per-point residual series, the placebo and re-derivation details by file name, the held-out curve list, and the specification of the bootstrap used in T5 (200 replicates, rho = 0.6).

review.overall_assessment: The record is complete in the sense that all three executed artifacts (dataset, literature screen, china-pot experiment) are written up and their headline numbers trace to executed outputs. I recomputed the headline values from the artifact files: C0 30-minute window RMS 1.067 K (analysis_results.json, method_out.json), C1 0.359 K, drawn model-1 curve 2.422 K, Table 2 full-record RSS/NDF values, the reproduction-gate ratios, the placebo result (median 0.028, max 0.186, p = 0.0099 in results/audit.json) and the 0.003 K re-derivation agreement all match the report. results_reported is therefore true. However, the record contains a claim that its own table contradicts: the report says the source's drawn model-1 curve shows the same early-under, late-over residual pattern as C0, but Table 1 and analysis_results.json give that curve positive residuals at every window point (+0.99 K mean over 0-10 min, +2.49 K mean over 20 min and later). That claim is repeated in the 'What we have learned' section and is used to read the failed T6 check as real misfit, so soundness is scored 1 and the record is blocking. Other problems: the sentence that the constant-rate law 'fits the whole record well only when T_room is free' is contradicted by Table 2 (RSS/NDF 0.84 K^2, about chi2/NDF 9 at sigma 0.3 C); the headline 1.1 K misfit depends on an ambient temperature the source does not report and that the report's own sensitivity fit halves to 0.54 K; the 'late' residual shape rests on one window point (25.9 min, -2.03 K); the reproduction-gate targets (32.1, 2.4, 81.3, 1.0) have no located source in the record; and the question asked, how accurately Newton's law predicts a 30-minute coffee cup compared with published measurements, is answered only in-sample for one curve while the eight-curve held-out set is unscored, so coverage is partial.
strengths: Every executed artifact is reported, including the dead ends: the screen's blocked sources, the failed reproduction gate, the failed T5 bootstrap coverage and T6 digitization check, the excluded Langer and Sedlacek curves, and the unidentifiable evaporation term.

Headline numbers are traceable and reproduce from the artifacts: C0 and C1 window RMS, bootstrap intervals, AIC/BIC, the full-record fits in Table 2, the sensitivity fits (C0 ambient 35 C, RMS 0.54 K; C1 ambient 30 C, x = 1.50), the forecast check and the placebo p-value.

Limits are stated plainly and repeatedly: in-sample on seven points, one curve, the selection rule not applied after the gate failed, T5 showing the bootstrap intervals are probably too narrow, and the humidity, fat-layer and geometry tests not testable from the sources.

The independent re-derivation from the raw PDF with a different integrator and optimizer (agreement within 0.003 K) and the permutation placebo are both recorded, which is a stronger check than the run's own fit.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration: a standardized benchmark of published cooling curves with per-source variable coverage (dataset); a ranked comparison of five cooling candidates on the Sedláček and Dolejší curves with a stated selection rule, bootstrap intervals, and a residual-versus-time test of the constant-rate law (experiment); and a literature table saying which sources report humidity or mass loss, and whether the humidity claim has any published test (research). The surviving candidate is not yet confirmed: confirmation on the benchmark's held-out sources is the next iteration's first task. If no candidate beats the constant-rate law, the iteration reports that the simple law is adequate for this source and what fails, which is itself a finding about the 30-minute window.
strategies.objective: Establish how accurately Newton's law of cooling predicts open-cup coffee temperature over 30 minutes, by screening the five candidate models on the same published cooling curves and confirming the surviving model on held-out sources. The contribution is a ranked, honestly reported comparison of the constant-rate law with its nonlinear-convection, evaporative and geometry-threshold corrections, measured against published data rather than asserted.
strategies.rationale: The user asks how well Newton's law matches published measurements, so the work has to compare the law with curves that exist in print. Iteration 1 has no prior artifacts, and the hypothesis carries three alternates that answer the same question by different mechanisms. The run cannot collect new laboratory curves (its executors are compute and web agents, not physical instruments), so the evidence is published curves, digitized and standardized. The shift from the literal question is only in the instrument: the main hypothesis asks about humidity, which the one well-documented source (Sedláček and Dolejší) does not report. Testing humidity therefore needs a source that reports it, and the research slot is set up to look for one rather than assume it. Positive outcomes are the target: the power law in temperature already reaches chi2/NDF near 1 in the Sedláček and Dolejší fit, so a corrected law that beats the constant-rate law on held-out sources is a realistic lead result.

artifacts.layman_summary: We fit two simple cooling formulas to one measured coffee cooling curve, then checked how well they predict other published curves over 30 minutes; the one that fits its own curve misses others by several degrees.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_2
artifacts.summary: This artifact fits two cooling laws to the first 30 minutes of one published coffee cooling curve (a china-pot measurement from Sedlacek and Dolejsi, 2010). C0 is Newton's law of cooling with a constant rate, T(t) = Tr + (T0 - Tr) exp(-k t). C1 is a one-term nonlinear convection law, dT/dt = -kc (T - Tr)^x, with kc and x fitted, since only kc is identifiable from a cooling curve. Parameters are then frozen and scored, by 30-minute root-mean-square error (RMS, in K), on a Manitoba workshop coffee table curve and six Langer hot-water curves, and a leave-one-source-out protocol refits the models on the other two sources in turn. Room temperature is handled two ways: recorded where a source reports it (Manitoba 21.67 C), and a 20 C default flagged where none is reported (Sedlacek and Langer), with a second ambient in which room temperature is a fitted shared parameter bounded to 5 K around a reference. Intervals are bootstraps with 1000 resamples and seed 0: between-curve where a set has two or more curves, and within-curve block bootstrap (block length 3) for single curves, which are labelled as not comparable. The C1 closed form is cross-checked against scipy solve_ivp (LSODA) to 1.6e-6 K. Headline results, ambient A: in-sample RMS 1.26 K for C0 and 0.33 K for C1 on the fitting curve (the earlier in-sample figure, 1.07 K, was not reproduced for C0, and C1 reproduces at 0.36 K); out of sample, Manitoba RMS is 3.45 K (C0) and 2.66 K (C1); the six Langer curves average 9.15 K (C0) and 9.06 K (C1); across all seven held-out curves the means are 8.33 K and 8.14 K. The pre-registered accuracy target (under 0.5 K) is not met, and the early-window residual sign prediction for C0 fails on the Langer curves. An independent re-derivation from the raw data, using solve_ivp for C1 rather than the closed form, reproduces every stored RMS and signed residual within 1.2e-6 K. A sign-flip placebo shows the paired C1 advantage (mean difference -0.19 K, C1 lower on 5 of 7 curves) is not statistically supported (p = 0.0625 for the mean; 0.23 for the count under no difference). Limits: eight curves from three sources, with the six Langer curves from one lab and protocol; no humidity or fat-layer data, so evaporation is untested; several fits end on parameter bounds, which are flagged in the outputs; and the Langer 65 C crossing-time disagreement is carried as metadata only. A sensitivity extension scores all ten digitized Langer curves with the frozen planned parameters (12-example full_method_out.json; planned headline numbers unchanged). Outputs are results/heldout_scores.json, results/fold_summary.json and results/method_out.json (with mini and preview variants), and these result files stay on the run volume rather than in the published repository.
artifacts.title: Newton cooling law tested on held-out coffee curves

artifacts.layman_summary: Checks whether the simple cooling law for coffee, with its fitted power term, predicts measured cup temperatures better than plain Newton cooling over 30 minutes, using published curves.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_3
artifacts.summary: Experiment artifact testing whether the fitted exponent x of the one-term nonlinear cooling law dT/dt = -a (T - T_room)^x / C is a stable quantity or an artifact of a free power fitted to about seven in-window points. Newton's law of cooling (C0, the x = 1 member) is the baseline. Inputs: full_data_out.json from dataset art_-CfKbDAPDpKm (8 curves, 3 source folds; 4 more Langer curves digitized in that artifact are added here). Method: closed-form fits on the china-pot first 30 minutes; fixed-x fits at x = 1.00, 1.25, 1.34, 1.50; a profile over x on a 1.00 to 3.00 grid (plan grid to 2.00 was extended because its minimum sat at the edge); free-x fits; a 200-replicate moving-block bootstrap. Held-out scoring on Manitoba and ten Langer curves (twelve curves in total) under S1 (strict transfer of a) and S2 (refit a on 0 to 10 minutes, score 10 to 30). Headline results: in-window profile minimum x = 2.18 with a delta-chi-squared 3.84 interval [1.95, 2.42] (sigma 0.3 C); bootstrap median 2.21, 95% interval [2.03, 2.36]; C0 in-window RMS 1.26 K. Held-out: S1 is scorable only for Manitoba (C0 3.66 K, x = 2.18 2.82 K) because Langer room temperatures are not reported; S2 mean RMS over eleven usable curves (Manitoba plus ten Langer cups) is 0.64 K for C0 and 0.60 K at x = 2.18, but C1 beats C0 on only 2 of 11 curves at x = 2.18 (nine of ten Langer curves are worse). Benchmark gate FAILED: the prior-round targets (C0 1.07 K; x = 1.94 with 0.36 K) were not reproduced under either initial-temperature convention; the cause (digitization or window) is unresolved. Reproduction-gate values: 32.1, 2.4 and 1.0 found near chi in the source PDF text; 81.3 unverified; gate status conditional. An independent ODE-based re-derivation agrees with the headline numbers, and a shuffled-time placebo gives 13.5 K RMS. Limits: seven points, twelve curves (eight from the dataset plus four digitized Langer curves added in this run), three sources, no humidity or fat-layer series, scale-dependent parameters; the exponent may absorb evaporation. Outputs: results/exponent_profile.json, results/heldout_scores.json, results/gate_provenance.json, results/benchmark_checks.json, method_out.json with full, mini and preview variants.
artifacts.title: Testing the cooling exponent for coffee

artifacts.layman_summary: This artifact recovers the temperature of a cooling cup of coffee over about 140 minutes from a published physics paper's figure, arranged as a machine-readable dataset. It finds no published record that also logs humidity or cup mass over time.
artifacts.name: gen_art_dataset_2
artifacts.summary: Dataset of one measured hot-liquid cooling curve: coffee in a china pot, digitised from Fig. 1 of Sedlacek & Dolejsi (American Journal of Physics, preprint PDF). The curve has 29 points from -0.3 to 138.6 min, read from the PDF's vector markers. Axes were calibrated from tick-label centres, with calibration residuals of 0.06 min in time and 0.21 C in temperature, below the 0.5 C acceptance limit. The paper's stated thermometer error of 0.3 C is the reference. Each example is one time point: the input holds time and the fields the source does not state (initial and room temperature, relative humidity, cup mass, pot geometry, lid), each set to null, and the output is the liquid temperature. The metal-pot, vacuum-pot and water-with-fat curves are not published as curves in the paper, so they are not included. A search of 14 queries across 6 readable sources (4 further sources returned HTTP 403) found no series recording humidity, vapour pressure, evaporation rate or cup mass with the cooling curve; this is an absence in what was searched, not proof that none exists. The Langer 2018 Zenodo record has no raw series and is excluded. The source PDF is fetched with TLS verification disabled because its host serves an incomplete certificate chain. The data validate against exp_sel_data_out with zero schema errors using jsonschema directly; the aii-json CLI refused the workspace path and returned no detail.

critiques.description: The 0.54 K free-ambient constant-rate RMS in stage 1 (Analysis 1 of the window results, the sensitivity paragraph) is not reproduced by any stage 2 artifact and I could not locate it in the stage 1 or stage 2 result files. The report keeps it in the stage 1 text with a correction and lists it as a dead end, but it is still an untraceable number inside the record.
critiques.suggested_action: Search the stage 1 artifact (art_UaVOg91elcVt) result files for the free-ambient window fit and cite the file and key where it comes from. If it cannot be found, delete the number from the stage 1 text and say the value was claimed without a trace, rather than leaving it as a dead end with a number.

critiques.description: The stage 1 constant-rate headline (1.07 K, Table 1 and the Stage 1 text) is traceable to art_UaVOg91elcVt but is not reproduced by the stage 2 artifacts, which give 1.26 K with T_room at 20 C on the re-read curve. The correction says the 1.07 K 'holds only with room temperature fixed at 20 C' and then states that stage 2 does not match it at that setting. The record therefore contradicts itself on whether the figure holds.
critiques.suggested_action: Rewrite the correction to state one fact: at T_room = 20 C the stage 1 artifact gives 1.07 K and the stage 2 re-read gives 1.26 K, the difference is unexplained, and the reading time shift (-0.30 min in gate_provenance.json) is the first candidate cause. Remove the phrase that the figure 'holds'. Keep Table 1 but label its digitization.

critiques.description: The Langer ten-curve sensitivity extension (results/sensitivity_langer10.json in art_-CfKbDAPDpKm / art_YY3zHfdcKluB) is described in one sentence ('the main numbers do not change') with no table. The independent re-derivation output (audit/rederive_output.txt) is summarized as a bound (1.2e-6 K) with no per-curve comparison. Both are executed outputs whose numbers the reader cannot see.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a table for the ten-curve sensitivity extension with per-curve 30-minute RMS and mean signed deviation for C0 and C1 under the frozen parameters, and a table of the re-derivation comparison with stored and recomputed RMS per curve. Cite each file by its path relative to the artifact.

critiques.description: The original question asks how accurately Newton's law predicts a coffee cup over 30 minutes compared with published measurements. The record answers this in-sample on one coffee curve (seven window points) and out of sample on one coffee curve (Manitoba). Coverage of the request is partial; the report's summary of what 'survives' is appropriately narrow, but no accuracy figure for coffee in general is given.
critiques.suggested_action: Keep the summary's narrow claim and state coverage as partial in the record. Name the missing part explicitly: out-of-sample accuracy on more than one coffee curve with recorded room temperature. Do not add a general coffee accuracy figure until such a curve is scored.

critiques.description: The stage 2 transfer claim that 'the reduction is the largest effect in the held-out set' rests on the Manitoba curve alone. Under the fit scheme (Table 13) the nonlinear law at x = 2.18 is worse than the constant-rate fit on nine of ten Langer curves, and the planned mean criterion passes only with a sign-flip placebo p of 0.0625. The claim is stronger than the record supports.
critiques.suggested_action: Replace the sentence with a statement limited to the single coffee curve, and state the Langer result (worse on nine of ten under the fit scheme) in the same sentence. Note that the mean criterion passes at the planned threshold while its placebo p is 0.0625.

critiques.description: The statement that the constant-rate law is 'warm by 2 to 5 K at every point in the window' on the Manitoba curve has no per-point table in the report, so the reader cannot check the per-point range against the artifact.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the per-point signed deviations for the Manitoba curve under C0 and C1 (from the held-out artifact's per-curve output) to Table 7 or a new table, or remove the per-point range.

critiques.description: Two stage 1 validation statements are not traced to the file that holds them. The placebo and the independent re-derivation are attributed to art_UaVOg91elcVt with no file name (the placebo values are in results/tests.json and results/audit.json), and the bootstrap replicate count for T5 is not stated. The sentence that the re-derivation matches 'the main window RMS values to within 0.003 K' does not say that the 0.003 K covers the published curve only (2.419 against 2.422), not the fitted models.
critiques.suggested_action: Name results/audit.json, results/tests.json and results/analysis_results.json where each claim appears. State the T5 bootstrap replicate count. Say that the 0.003 K agreement is for the published curve values and that the fitted models agree to 0.00002 K.

critiques.description: The held-out curve table (Table 5) gives first recorded temperatures and roles but not sample counts or time spans, which the next iteration needs to identify its test set from the record alone. The Langer 65 C crossing-time disagreement is stated for the Langer group but not flagged per curve.
critiques.suggested_action: Add sample count and time span columns to Table 5 for all eleven curves, and flag each Langer row with the unresolved crossing-time disagreement.

critiques.description: Table 9 marks 'C1 beats C0 on the held-out mean' as pass. The mean difference is -0.19 K with a sign-flip placebo p of 0.0625, and the LOSO fit reverses the sign on Manitoba. A pass recorded against an unstated threshold reads as stronger support than the placebo supports.
critiques.suggested_action: State the threshold used for the pass in the criteria table, and place the placebo p beside the pass in the same cell.

critiques.description: The positive in-sample result (nonlinear law fits the 30-minute window better) is compared with Vollmer (2009) and the source's own model, and the record says the stage adds a single-curve quantification and a negative scope result. This comparison is adequate. The held-out advantage is not compared with any published held-out test of a nonlinear cooling law, because none was searched for in stage 2.
critiques.suggested_action: State in the contribution paragraph that no published held-out test of a nonlinear convection law on coffee was searched for in stage 2, so the reader knows the comparison is limited to the in-sample neighbour.

dimension_scores.justification: Stage 2 headline numbers recompute from their artifacts, but stage 1 numbers are still carried with prose corrections rather than resolved. The 1.07 K figure is traceable to the stage 1 artifact yet not reproduced in stage 2, and its correction contradicts itself. The 0.54 K free-ambient figure has no artifact I could locate. The 'largest effect' claim for the nonlinear law overreaches a single coffee curve.

The record is ordered by stage and each analysis states its method, but some tables are introduced without saying what they settle, and the stage 1 and stage 2 numbers are interleaved with correction markers that a reader must reconcile.

The run preserves its experiments, failed gates and dead ends, and the held-out testing is a real addition. However, several executed outputs (the Langer ten-curve sensitivity extension, the independent re-derivation output, the 29-point re-read series) are not tabulated, and the stage adds little beyond the source paper and Vollmer.

review.overall_assessment: The record is largely traceable and most of the stage 2 headline numbers recompute from the artifacts. I recomputed the in-sample C0 RMS (1.2608 K) and C1 RMS (0.3275 K) and the paired difference (-0.933 K) from fold_summary.json; the held-out means (C0 8.335 K, C1 8.142 K over seven curves; Langer-only 9.149 and 9.056 K; eleven-curve means 0.641 and 0.603 K) from the per-curve values in Tables 7 and 13; the exponent profile minimum (x = 2.18, RMS 0.3275 K) from exponent_profile.json; and the stage 1 reproduction-gate values from gate_provenance.json. All of these match the report. The record is honest about failed gates, bound-hitting fits, the unresolved agreement test, and the non-significant held-out advantage. Problems remain. (1) Stage 1 headline numbers are kept in the record with corrections in prose rather than being resolved: the 1.07 K constant-rate RMS is traceable to the stage 1 artifact but is not reproduced by the stage 2 artifacts (1.26 K at the same 20 C setting), and the correction sentence says the 1.07 K figure 'holds only with T_room fixed at 20 C' while the same paragraph says stage 2 does not match it at that setting. The 0.54 K free-ambient value could not be located in any artifact read. (2) Several executed outputs are described in one sentence without their tables: the Langer ten-curve sensitivity extension (results/sensitivity_langer10.json), the independent re-derivation output (audit/rederive_output.txt), and the 29-point re-read series. (3) Some scope claims go beyond the evidence: 'the reduction is the largest effect in the held-out set' rests on one coffee curve, and the nonlinear law is worse than the constant-rate law on nine of ten Langer curves under the fit scheme. (4) The question asked for accuracy over 30 minutes compared with published measurements; the record answers it in-sample on one curve and out-of-sample on one coffee curve, so coverage is partial.
strengths: Headline stage 2 numbers recompute exactly from the artifact result files (fold_summary.json, exponent_profile.json, heldout_scores.json, gate_provenance.json), including the transfer means in Table 8 and the eleven-curve means in Table 13.

Negative results are kept and labelled: the failed reproduction gate, the failed T3, T5 and T6 checks, the failed 0.5 K accuracy target, the non-significant sign-flip placebo (p = 0.0625), and the bound-hitting fits.
The exponent instability is recorded as its own finding with a table of fits (Table 11), and the implication for claiming the nonlinear law is stated.
Stage 1 errors are corrected in place with dated correction markers rather than silently rewritten, preserving the chronology.
The novelty comparison against Vollmer (2009) and the source paper's own nonlinear model is written out and states what the stage does not add.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration: an out-of-sample 30-minute RMS for the constant-rate law and the nonlinear law on the held-out Manitoba and Langer curves, with the transfer and leave-one-source-out protocols, ambient choices, bootstrap intervals and per-curve residuals (experiment); a profile of the exponent x with fixed-exponent held-out scores and a provenance record for the reproduction-gate values (experiment); and a benchmark extension with per-series variable coverage and any readable metal, vacuum or fat series (dataset). If the held-out scores show C1 is no better than C0, that is the answer for these curves, and the paper says the constant-rate law is adequate at this window, or that it fails by a stated margin.
strategies.objective: Establish how accurately Newton's law of cooling predicts open-cup hot-liquid temperature over 30 minutes on published curves not used for fitting, and whether a nonlinear convective correction lowers held-out error, with the ambient and exponent assumptions made explicit. The contribution is an out-of-sample 30-minute error for the constant-rate law beside its in-sample figure, a check of whether the nonlinear exponent is a stable quantity or a flexible fit, and a first geometry or evaporation series wherever the published record allows one.
strategies.rationale: The user asks how accurately Newton's law predicts a cup of coffee over 30 minutes compared with published measurements. The only executed result so far is in-sample on one curve (C0 30-minute RMS 1.07 K at room temperature 20 C, 0.54 K with room temperature freed; C1 0.36 K, permutation p = 0.01), and the reviewer correctly says it is not an accuracy figure. The eight-curve held-out set exists on disk and has not been scored, so this iteration moves directly onto it. Its main experiment answers the accuracy and the comparison questions with out-of-sample numbers, and a second experiment attacks the unstable exponent (x = 1.50 to 1.94 across fits), which is the strongest reviewer objection to C1 as a model. The third slot is the cover slot: it reads the Sedlacek and Dolejsi metal and vacuum pot series and the water-with-fat series if the figures carry data, and it searches for published curves that log humidity or cup mass. This is the only route to the geometry and evaporation parts of the question with the evidence available. The shift from the previous plan is in scope: the held-out test is now the main object, and humidity stays a search rather than a claimed test. Report-level fixes the reviewer asked for (conditioning the 1.1 K figure on room temperature, the late-sign single point, the drawn-curve pattern, the Vollmer comparison, bibliography entries) are writing tasks that rest on the record and are not artifacts here.
strategies.title: Held-out test of nonlinear cooling law
